content.text:
I listed the documents and read the four that could matter. None of them has the data needed to check the 97% efficiency requirement at 2e16 neq/cm².

**Documents:** candidate_specs.md, meeting_notes_2026-03-02.md, readout_chip.md, schedule.md, services.md and simulation_summary_2025.md. I did not open schedule.md or services.md, because their names don't suggest anything on radiation damage, charge collection or bias.

**What the documents give:**
- **candidate_specs.md:**
  - T1 is a thin-pitch sensor with large signal sharing.
  - T2 is a planar sensor with standard pitch.
  - T3 is a 3D-electrode sensor with larger pitch.
  - All three can be bump bonded to the readout chip.
  - It gives no thickness ranges, pixel pitch values or bias limits.
- **readout_chip.md:** the common chip supports 50×50 µm² pixels and a hit rate of 1.5 GHz/cm². All three candidates are compatible.
- **simulation_summary_2025.md:** unirradiated single-hit resolution at 150 µm is 6.0 µm for T1, 9.0 µm for T2 and 14.0 µm for T3.
- **meeting_notes_2026-03-02.md:** it only covers cooling (CO2 evaporative at −35 °C) and mechanics, so it has nothing on sensors.

**What is missing:** I found no hit-efficiency data or model at 2e16 neq/cm², and no information on trapping, depletion or bias limits. The later steps will therefore have to find another way to establish the efficiency constraint. The simulation tool returns unirradiated resolution only. Choosing T1 because it has the best unirradiated resolution would not be supported by the documents.

I recorded the three 2025 resolutions and the chip's 50 µm pixel size and 1.5 GHz/cm² hit rate. I also recorded flags of 0 for "efficiency data found" and "bias limit data found".

content.text:
I couldn't build a feasible candidate list from the documents. None of them has the data needed to judge the 97% efficiency requirement at 2e16 neq/cm².

I read all six project documents. This is what they contain:
- **candidate_specs.md:** one-line descriptions of T1 (thin pitch, large signal sharing), T2 (planar, standard pitch) and T3 (3D electrodes, larger pitch). All three can be bump bonded.
- **readout_chip.md:** 50×50 µm² pixels and a 1.5 GHz/cm² hit rate. All candidates are compatible.
- **simulation_summary_2025.md:** unirradiated resolution at 150 µm of 6.0 µm for T1, 9.0 µm for T2 and 14.0 µm for T3.
- **meeting_notes_2026-03-02.md:** CO2 cooling at −35 °C is confirmed, and the carbon-fibre staves are on schedule.
- **services.md:** a 7 W power budget per module, with serial powering as the baseline.
- **schedule.md:** the sensor market survey closes in Q2 and pre-production is in Q4.

The documents give no hit threshold, no signal or charge-collection data after trapping, no bias voltage limit, and no efficiency data for irradiated sensors. They say nothing about how thickness affects end-of-life efficiency.

Because of this, I can't exclude any technology or thickness. I also can't confirm that any combination meets the hard requirement anywhere in 50–300 µm. Any feasible range I gave would be my own assumption, not something the documents support. For now, all three technologies across 50–300 µm are unconfirmed.

I recorded the requirement (97%), the fluence (2e16), the thickness bounds (50–300 µm) and flags showing that no efficiency, bias, threshold or trapping data exist. I did not record a feasible range.

The next step needs one of two things. One option is to get this data from the user or from external sources. The other is to explicitly adopt assumptions, such as typical literature values for trapping and bias limits. The final recommendation would then depend on those assumptions and should say so.

content.text:
I simulated all three technologies at 50, 100, 200 and 300 µm, but I could not tell which of those points meet the 97% efficiency requirement. The six project documents have no efficiency, trapping, bias or threshold data at 2e16 neq/cm². So none of these results are confirmed feasible, and I did not label any option as infeasible. The simulation is also unirradiated, so it says nothing about efficiency at end of life.

Single-hit resolution in µm, unirradiated:

| Thickness | T1 | T2 | T3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 50 µm | 6.77 | 10.19 | 15.61 |
| 100 µm | 6.07 | 9.56 | 14.77 |
| 200 µm | 6.44 | 9.91 | 14.43 |
| 300 µm | 7.71 | 11.71 | 19.29 |

- **Ranking:** T1 is best at every thickness, then T2, then T3.
- **Thickness trend:** T1 and T2 are best at about 100 µm. T3 is best at 200 µm, though it is nearly as good at 100 µm. All three are worst at 300 µm.
- **Earlier 150 µm results:** the 2025 values of 6, 9 and 14 µm fit between these points.

I recorded all 12 resolutions. I also recorded flags showing that the feasible range was not determined from the documents and that efficiency feasibility was not verified. The final recommendation will need an efficiency source, or a clearly stated assumption, before it can claim to meet the hard requirement.

content.text:
My pick is Sensor-T1 at 100 µm, but it is provisional. Nothing I have shows that it meets the 97% efficiency requirement at 2e16 neq/cm².

- **Efficiency:** None of the project documents has efficiency, trapping, threshold or bias-limit data for any technology at 2e16 neq/cm². I did not check the schedule and services documents myself. The earlier step reviewed all six and found no such data either. I therefore could not screen the candidates for feasibility, and I did not treat any of them as verified.
- **Resolution:** I compared the unirradiated simulation results. T1 is best at every thickness, and its best point is 100 µm at 6.07 µm. Its other thicknesses give 6.44 µm at 200 µm, 6.77 µm at 50 µm and 7.71 µm at 300 µm. T2 is best at 9.56 µm (100 µm) and T3 at 14.43 µm (200 µm). A thickness near 100 µm is also a sensible compromise for end-of-life charge collection, since thick sensors lose more signal to trapping.
- **Irradiated resolution:** I did not check it, because no irradiated simulation was available. Resolution will probably degrade after irradiation, and the T1 lead could shrink or disappear.

The main uncertainty is that T1 is a thin-pitch sensor, and I could not confirm it survives 2e16 neq/cm² at 97% efficiency. If T1 fails that requirement, the fallback is T3, a 3D-electrode sensor. That is only a general expectation about 3D sensors, not something the documents support. Before submitting, someone needs to get end-of-life efficiency data for T1, or run an irradiated simulation.

I recorded the thickness (100 µm), the unirradiated resolution (6.073 µm), and flags marking the choice as unverified.

content.text:
**Final submission (provisional): Sensor-T1 at 100 µm.** The 97% end-of-life efficiency requirement is not verified.

**Result**
- The simulated unirradiated single-hit resolution is **6.07 µm**.
- T1's resolution over the thickness scan was 6.77 µm at 50 µm, 6.07 µm at 100 µm, 6.44 µm at 200 µm and 7.71 µm at 300 µm.
- T1 has the best resolution at every thickness I simulated.
- The 2025 summary at 150 µm agrees on the ranking: T1 6.0 µm, T2 9.0 µm, T3 14.0 µm.

**Efficiency at 2e16 neq/cm² (hard requirement ≥97%)**
- I found no evidence that any candidate meets this requirement.
- I read all six project documents. None gives efficiency, trapping, threshold, bias-voltage limit or irradiated-performance data.
- The simulation covers only unirradiated sensors.
- The documents only say that all candidates are bump-bondable and compatible with the 50×50 µm² readout chip at 1.5 GHz/cm². The cooling is CO2 at -35 °C and the power budget is 7 W per module.

**Rejected alternatives**
- **T2 (planar, standard pitch):** best resolution 9.56 µm at 100 µm, about 57% worse than T1.
- **T3 (3D electrodes, larger pitch):** best resolution 14.4 µm at 200 µm, more than twice as bad as T1.
- Neither was rejected on efficiency grounds, because no efficiency data exists for any candidate. T3 might be more radiation-tolerant, since 3D sensors usually are, but nothing in the documents supports that.

**Caveats**
- **Efficiency is the main gap.** T1's large charge sharing and thin pitch may lose signal after irradiation, and I could not check this. Someone needs to supply irradiated efficiency data or run an irradiated simulation for T1 before this is final. If T1 fails at 2e16, the fallback is T2 or T3, whichever passes.
- **Thickness choice:** I picked 100 µm because it gave the best simulated resolution. Thinner sensors usually trap less charge after irradiation, but I did not test that.
- **Resolution is unirradiated.** Irradiation will change it, and I did not check by how much.
- **Thickness scan:** I simulated only 50, 100, 200 and 300 µm. The optimum could lie between those points, and 100 µm is the best of the points I ran.
